# hinge

A desktop scrcpy client that shows a Galaxy Z Fold 7 as a 3D phone that folds with the real one

## Development setup

No published releases yet. From a checkout of this repository:

```sh
npm install
npm run fetch-vendor
```

`fetch-vendor` downloads and checksums the bundled `adb` (Android platform-tools
r37.0.1) and `scrcpy-server-v4.1` into `vendor/` (gitignored). Pass `--only win` or
`--only linux` to fetch one platform.

## Status

Early development, M4 (showcase view). The app connects to a phone over adb, starts scrcpy-server 4.1, and shows the video on a 3D model of the Fold 7 that folds, unfolds and turns with the real phone, with touch and keyboard input routed back to the device, in a flat work view or a 3D showcase view. Audio and packaged releases are later milestones.

## Running

```sh
npm run dev
```

connects to whatever device `adb` sees. Relevant flags:

- `--serial <id>` pick a device when more than one is attached
- `--replay <file.hrec>` play back a recorded session instead of a live device
- `--record <file.hrec>` mirror a live device and also write the session (video
  and posture samples) to a recording file
- `--probe` run a one-off hardware survey: waits for a device, collects `adb`
  property and `dumpsys` output, checks the scrcpy display list, and samples
  `device_state`/rotation while you fold and rotate the phone. Writes a JSON
  report to the desktop, or to the path given with `--out <file>`
- `--seconds <n>` how long `--probe` samples for (default 90)

A bare file name given to `--record` or `--out` (no directory in the path)
lands on the desktop; a path with a directory is used as given.

Each run writes `hinge.log` to the app's logs directory (truncated at
startup, no rotation) with server output, connection attempts and errors.
An error shown in the window or the probe result page names the log file.

### Folding

The window shows the phone at a constant physical size (the body fills 85
percent of the screen's height) and follows the phone as you fold it:

- Closed or tented, you see the cover screen. Open it and the model unfolds
  to the inner screen; close it and it folds back. The hinge starts moving
  as soon as the phone reports the new posture, and the video moves to the
  other screen once the phone's stream restarts at that screen's size.
- The window keeps its height and grows or shrinks sideways, anchored on
  the right edge (the half with the cameras), so the phone doesn't jump
  around the desktop. It covers both poses while the hinge moves and trims
  to the final size afterwards.
- Half open (Flex mode) with the inner screen on, the model stays flat and
  shows a small "Flex" badge on the top bezel.
- Turn the phone to landscape and the model turns with it around the
  window's centre; touches still land where you click on the video.

### Showcase view

Left Alt+D (or left Super+D) switches between the flat work view and a 3D
showcase view, easing the camera and the window size over 600 ms; press it
again mid-way to turn back from where it is.

- The showcase looks at the phone from a three-quarter angle, slightly from
  above, lit by a studio environment, with a soft shadow under it and a
  glass reflection on the screens. It shows the phone's real posture:
  tented, half open or flat.
- Dragging on the lit screen still touches the phone. Dragging anywhere
  else turns the phone around; two seconds after you let go it eases back.
- Shift+drag off the screen moves the window, since a plain drag turns the
  phone there.
- Back in the work view the camera and window are exactly as before.

### Windows

From a `cmd.exe` prompt in the installed or unpacked directory:

```bat
hinge.exe --serial 10.0.0.23:5555
hinge.exe --probe --seconds 60
```

The window is frameless; close it with Alt+F4 or from the taskbar.

## Development commands

```sh
npm run dev          # electron-vite dev server
npm run build         # production build
npm run typecheck     # tsc -b
npm test              # vitest
npm run test:e2e       # playwright, replays a synthetic fold recording end to end
npm run pack:win       # unpacked Windows build in dist/win-unpacked
npm run pack:linux     # unpacked Linux build in dist/linux-unpacked
```

### Remote testing

The dev container has no GPU, so `npm run test:e2e` here runs under Xvfb with
SwiftShader software GL, which is slow and skips the app's lighting and
reflections. `HINGE_REMOTE=<ssh alias> scripts/e2e-remote.sh [playwright
args]` rsyncs the working tree to a host with a real GPU, installs
dependencies there only when `package-lock.json` changed, builds, runs the
suite against the real display with `HINGE_E2E_REAL_GPU=1` set (the test
skips its SwiftShader flags when that's set), and copies `test-results/`
back under `test-results/remote-<host>/`. On a macOS host the test step runs
as a self-owned LaunchAgent bootstrapped into the logged-in user's GUI
session rather than being spawned straight from the ssh shell, since a
plain ssh session can't reach the WindowServer and fixing that with
`launchctl asuser` needs root.

Set `HINGE_REAL_RECORDING=<file.hrec>` to also replay a real `--record`
capture; that test passes once it has seen the model settle on the inner
screen after the cover and back again. `HINGE_REAL_RECORDING_TIMEOUT_MS`
(default 180000) bounds how long it waits.

`HINGE_ADB_REMOTE=<ssh alias> scripts/adb-remote.sh start|stop|status`
forwards a local port to another host's adb server over ssh, for a phone
that's only reachable from there (wireless debugging paired to a different
machine). `start` opens a background tunnel from `127.0.0.1:15037` here to
`127.0.0.1:5037` on the host, `status` runs `adb -H 127.0.0.1 -P 15037
devices` through it, and `stop` closes it; it never starts, stops, or
restarts an adb server anywhere.
